_comment: Regression floors for `python evals/golden_eval.py gate`, enforced in CI.
These are FLOORS, not targets. Each is set just below the measured value at
the time it was added, so the gate catches a regression without pretending
the current number is good. Raise a floor when the metric genuinely improves;
never lower one to make a red build green.
Metrics not computed in a run are reported as SKIP, never as a pass.

_measured.note: One paper is not a benchmark. These floors are placeholders that become meaningful at 40+ papers.

grounding_precision._why: Measured 0.533. A false positive is a fabricated claim shown to the user as verified, so this is the number that matters most and the one most in need of improvement.

grounding_recall._why: Measured 1.000. Recall is cheap here because the guard passes almost everything; a drop would mean true claims are being flagged.

section_detection._why: Measured 0.800 on one paper. The 2026-07-07 benchmark saw 50% on abstract/methodology across eight, so expect this to fall as the set grows.

degenerate_rate._why: The 2026-07-07 run produced 25% degenerate summaries under free-tier pressure. Requires --predictions; SKIPped otherwise.

numeric_fidelity._why: Never measured. Requires --predictions. Placeholder until a prediction set exists.
